# doit_custom_metric (Resource)

Manages a custom metric: a formula over the costs, usage, savings or extended metrics of single allocations, such as cost per ride. Reports, alerts and allocation splits can use it as a metric.

~> **Note:** Custom metrics require the calculated metrics entitlement. A custom metric that a report, an alert or an allocation uses cannot be deleted; remove it from them first.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Variables measure single allocations.
resource "doit_allocation" "gcp" {
  name        = "Google Cloud"
  description = "All Google Cloud costs"
  rule = {
    formula = "A"
    components = [
      { key = "cloud_provider", mode = "is", type = "fixed", values = ["google-cloud"] },
    ]
  }
}

resource "doit_allocation" "aws" {
  name        = "AWS"
  description = "All AWS costs"
  rule = {
    formula = "A"
    components = [
      { key = "cloud_provider", mode = "is", type = "fixed", values = ["amazon-web-services"] },
    ]
  }
}

# The Google Cloud share of the combined Google Cloud and AWS cost. The order
# of variables sets their letters: the first is A, the second B.
resource "doit_custom_metric" "gcp_share" {
  name        = "Google Cloud share"
  description = "Google Cloud cost as a percentage of Google Cloud and AWS cost"
  variables = [
    {
      metric        = { type = "basic", value = "cost" }
      allocation_id = doit_allocation.gcp.id
    },
    {
      metric        = { type = "basic", value = "cost" }
      allocation_id = doit_allocation.aws.id
    },
  ]
  formula   = "A / (A + B) * 100"
  unit_type = "percentage"
  decimals  = { min = 0, max = 2 }
}

# A variable can also measure an extended metric of the billing data source,
# such as amortized cost.
resource "doit_custom_metric" "aws_amortized_ratio" {
  name = "AWS amortized to billed cost"
  variables = [
    {
      metric        = { type = "extended", value = "amortized_cost" }
      allocation_id = doit_allocation.aws.id
    },
    {
      metric        = { type = "basic", value = "cost" }
      allocation_id = doit_allocation.aws.id
    },
  ]
  formula = "A / B"
}

# Reports use a custom metric by its ID.
resource "doit_report" "gcp_share" {
  name = "Google Cloud share"
  config = {
    metrics       = [{ type = "custom", value = doit_custom_metric.gcp_share.id }]
    aggregation   = "total"
    time_interval = "month"
    data_source   = "billing"
    dimensions    = [{ id = "month", type = "datetime" }]
    time_range = {
      mode            = "last"
      amount          = 3
      include_current = true
      unit            = "month"
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `formula` (String) Arithmetic over the variable letters: `A` for the first entry of `variables`, `B` for the second, up to `E`. Allowed are those letters, numbers such as `100` or `0.5`, the operators `+`, `-`, `*` and `/`, parentheses and spaces. The formula is stored exactly as written (`A / B` stays `A / B`). The API rejects a formula that does not parse, divides by a literal `0`, or uses a letter without a variable.
- `name` (String) Name of the custom metric. It must contain a character other than a space and is stored exactly as written.
- `variables` (Attributes List) The variables of the formula, 1 to 5. Their order sets their letters: the first is `A`, the second `B`, up to `E`. Reordering the list changes which variable a letter in `formula` refers to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variables))

### Optional

- `decimals` (Attributes) Number of decimal places reports show, from `min` to `max`. Omit it to use the reports' default formatting. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--decimals))
- `description` (String) Description of the custom metric. Defaults to an empty string.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `unit_type` (String) How reports show the value: a plain `number`, a `percentage`, or a `currency` amount in the customer's currency. Defaults to `number`.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the metric was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `etag` (String) Current ETag of the custom metric. The provider sends it with updates and deletes to detect changes made outside Terraform.
- `id` (String) The ID of the custom metric. Reports use it as `metric = { type = "custom", value = <id> }`.
- `owner` (String) Email address of the user or service account that created the custom metric. Only the owner can delete it.
- `update_time` (String) When the metric was last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).

<a id="nestedatt--variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variables`

Required:

- `allocation_id` (String) ID of the single allocation the variable measures, such as `doit_allocation.example.id`. A group allocation is rejected, and a preset allocation needs the preset allocations entitlement.
- `metric` (Attributes) The metric the variable measures. A custom metric cannot be a variable of another custom metric. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variables--metric))

Read-Only:

- `letter` (String) Letter of the variable in the formula, from its position: `A` for the first, up to `E`.

<a id="nestedatt--variables--metric"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variables.metric`

Required:

- `type` (String) `basic` for a cost, usage or savings metric. `extended` for an extended metric, such as a DataHub or GenAI metric.
Possible values: `basic`, `extended`
- `value` (String) For `basic`: `cost`, `usage` or `savings`. For `extended`: the key of an extended metric of the `billing` or `billing-datahub` data source, the same key a report uses with `type = "extended"`. The API rejects any other value.



<a id="nestedatt--decimals"></a>
### Nested Schema for `decimals`

Required:

- `max` (Number) Most decimal places shown. Not less than `min`.
- `min` (Number) Fewest decimal places shown. Not greater than `max`.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import doit_custom_metric.example [id]
```
